title: Proteome-scale prediction of molecular interactions and affinities

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a generalizable computational capability to predict which proteins interact with small molecules or other proteins, which pairs do not bind, where interacting partners contact one another, and how strongly they bind under specified conditions. Its intended scope includes unfamiliar protein families and molecular partners, as well as difficult disordered and membrane-associated targets. Proteome-scale coverage means making these predictions broadly enough, and at practical enough computational cost, to screen interactions across an organism’s protein repertoire. This is the proposed capability, not an achievement established by the supplied evidence.

Three distinct predictions must work together: whether binding occurs, the geometry of the bound complex, and binding affinity. A plausible predicted structure does not by itself establish a dependable affinity, and ranking affinities among known binders does not show that a model can distinguish binders from nonbinders. The supplied benchmark directly illustrates these distinctions for protein–ligand prediction; it does not evaluate the entire proposed range of partners and targets.

significance.text: If reliable generalization and practical computational costs were achieved, large interaction screens could help researchers prioritize which molecular pairs to test experimentally. The supplied study places protein–ligand affinity prediction within virtual screening, structure-based drug discovery and lead optimization. Extending dependable predictions across a proteome could make these workflows substantially more systematic, while still requiring experimental confirmation.

Conditional synthesis: dependable binding and nonbinding predictions could help identify candidate interaction partners and assess molecular selectivity across many proteins. Affinity estimates would add a quantitative basis for ranking those candidates, while interface predictions could guide experiments or molecular modifications. These benefits depend on coverage, uncertainty calibration and performance on unfamiliar inputs; the supplied benchmark does not demonstrate proteome-wide screening or its downstream benefits.

Impact boundary: molecular binding is only one component of biological function and drug performance. Even a successful interaction predictor would not by itself establish delivery to the relevant tissue or cellular compartment, safety, efficacy, or the consequences of an interaction in a living system. Computational screening could focus laboratory work, but the proposed innovation does not establish that most laboratory assays could be replaced.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability in the supplied evidence is dependable affinity prediction under the structural-input conditions encountered in deployment, together with discrimination between binding and nonbinding pairs. In the evaluated workflows, prediction quality depended on how the complex structure was obtained, and averaging predictions across multiple poses did not restore near-crystal performance for perturbed inputs. Better structural plausibility therefore cannot simply be assumed to deliver reliable interaction energetics.

Generalization is a separate barrier. All evaluated complexes were confirmed binders, so the study could not establish whether the models assign appropriately weaker affinities to nonbinding pairs. All benchmark structures also predated the AlphaFold3 training cutoff, limiting conclusions about deployment on unfamiliar targets. A broader capability needs evidence that its performance survives changes in protein family, partner chemistry and structural-input quality, rather than relying on familiar benchmark distributions.

Scientific and engineering synthesis: extending the capability to specified environmental conditions, protein partners, disordered regions and membrane-associated targets requires representing the molecular states and contexts that determine binding. Flexible conformations and alternative interfaces complicate the relationship between a single predicted pose and an observed affinity. Models would also need useful uncertainty estimates when these states or contexts are poorly determined. These are barriers implied by the intended scope; their severity and current degree of resolution are not established by the supplied protein–ligand study.

Engineering synthesis: proteome-scale usefulness additionally requires manageable computational costs, consistent handling of heterogeneous inputs, and predictions that remain useful when most screened pairs may not bind. The supplied evidence does not establish the throughput, coverage or error rates necessary for that operating regime.

current_state.text: Eaves and Woldring’s “Robustness of Protein–Ligand Binding Affinity Prediction Models to Docked and Predicted Structures,” dated June 23, 2026, evaluated five reproducible protein–ligand affinity prediction pipelines. Their performance depended on structural input. AlphaFold3 co-folding was competitive with docking into apo receptors and significantly better for two of the five pipelines. This establishes a useful result within the evaluated workflows, rather than a general demonstration of interaction or affinity prediction.

Multipose averaging had effects that depended on the source of the structures and did not recover near-crystal performance for any perturbed input in the study. This result concerns the evaluated pipelines and the tested averaging approach. It does not establish that every affinity method fails on predicted or docked structures, nor that future methods cannot overcome this sensitivity.

The evaluation used confirmed protein–ligand binders throughout, leaving binding-versus-nonbinding discrimination untested. Its CASF-2016 structures all predated the AlphaFold3 training cutoff. The article consequently cautions that the reported co-folding performance may be optimistic relative to deployment on targets absent from AlphaFold3’s training data. Predating the cutoff does not itself establish that every evaluated structure was in the training data, but it limits the strength of claims about unfamiliar-target generalization.

The supplied review reports verification of the full main-article HTML without truncation or reported extraction problems. Supplementary material and figure images were not inspected, so interpretations here are bounded by the main-text findings recorded in that review. The supplied record identifies a dated journal article and DOI, rather than a preprint; the principal qualifications concern evaluation scope and generalization.

Evidence boundary: the supplied material does not establish the field-wide state as of November 2026. The review’s bounded freshness-search record was empty, leaving subsequent advances unverified. It also does not independently substantiate the earlier broad characterization of AlphaFold3 as a major advance across complex structure prediction, or determine present capability across protein partners, disordered targets and membrane-associated targets. Those limitations do not invalidate the reported June 2026 findings or show that unexamined results are false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: conduct prospective, blinded evaluations spanning diverse protein families, small molecules and protein partners. Measure binding-versus-nonbinding discrimination, binding geometry where experimentally measurable, and affinity prediction with calibrated uncertainty as separate outcomes. Include difficult targets, held-out families and chemistries, and explicit assessment of disordered and membrane-associated targets. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, not established community standards.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: The benchmark directly motivates testing with structures representative of actual screening workflows: docking into apo or predicted receptors and co-folded predicted complexes. Evaluation should also include nonbinding pairs, addressing the study’s known-binder-only limitation. Performance on experimentally resolved complexes alone would leave these documented deployment questions unanswered.
completion_criteria.label: The benchmark directly motivates testing with structures representative

completion_criteria.text: Proposed assessment design: prespecify experimental conditions, operational definitions of binding and nonbinding, generalization splits, numerical success thresholds and uncertainty-calibration criteria. Compare performance with experimental uncertainty and relevant existing screening methods. Report results separately by target class and structural-input source so that aggregate performance does not conceal important failures. No numerical threshold is supplied here because the record does not establish an appropriate universal value.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed assessment design

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: provide sufficient methods, data and executable workflows for independent groups to repeat the evaluation, and seek confirmation on prospectively collected interactions. Report computational cost, throughput, coverage and failure rates at the intended screening scale. Successful finite tests would demonstrate breadth over the tested domains and conditions; they would not establish literal universality across every protein, partner or environment.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: BIF-02, “Predictive molecular dynamics from biological sequence,” has the closest overlap through molecular energetics and dynamics. BIF-09 retains a distinct goal: interaction screening and affinity prediction could be useful without general prediction of molecular trajectories or transition rates. Conversely, a dynamics capability would not automatically establish accurate binding-versus-nonbinding classification at screening scale.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-06, “A general decoder for unknown gene and protein functions,” could use predicted interaction partners as evidence about function, but binding alone does not establish a protein’s biological role. BIF-07, “Computational reconstruction of organism-scale molecular maps,” overlaps through interaction maps, while also requiring broader spatial and organism-level organization. BIF-04, “General reconstruction of causal cellular networks,” requires causal relationships that cannot be inferred from molecular binding alone.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-03, “A transferable, predictive virtual cell,” could incorporate interaction and affinity predictions as molecular inputs, but predicting whole-cell behavior requires additional capabilities. BIF-08, “Reliable reconstruction and forecasting of single-cell fates,” concerns changes in cellular state and developmental outcomes; interaction predictions could inform mechanisms without independently establishing those forecasts.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-01, “A predictive decoder for the regulatory genome,” overlaps where proteins interact with regulatory machinery, but its central task is predicting regulatory effects from genomic information. BIF-05, “Computer-aided design of functional whole genomes,” and BIF-13, “Predictive design of functional genetic circuits and pathways,” could use interaction predictions to evaluate components and unintended interactions. Their design goals additionally require coordinated function beyond pairwise molecular binding.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-10, “A broadly capable autonomous bioinformatics discovery system,” could use this capability within a larger discovery workflow; autonomy and broad scientific reasoning remain separate requirements. BIF-11, “Accessible, uncertainty-aware assembly of complex genomes,” addresses sequence reconstruction rather than molecular interaction prediction. BIF-12, “Strain-resolved discovery and functional profiling of microbial communities,” could draw on interaction predictions when interpreting microbial proteins, but also requires community composition, strain resolution and functional profiling.

change_log.change: Preserved BIF-09’s identity and broad intended scope while distinguishing that scope from demonstrated protein–ligand results.
change_log.reason: The narrower evidence does not justify deleting the concept or claiming that every intended target class has been evaluated.

change_log.change: Separated binding occurrence, complex geometry and affinity as distinct capabilities.
change_log.reason: Plausible structures and affinity rankings among known binders do not establish reliable nonbinding discrimination.

change_log.change: Expanded the dated benchmark account to include five pipelines, AlphaFold3’s relative performance, two significantly improved pipelines and the specific multipose-averaging result.
change_log.reason: These details preserve useful positive findings while limiting conclusions to the evaluated workflows.

change_log.change: Added the known-binder-only evaluation and training-cutoff qualification.
change_log.reason: They materially limit conclusions about negative screening and unfamiliar-target generalization; cutoff timing alone does not prove training-set membership.

change_log.change: Replaced broad field-wide claims about AlphaFold3 and present-day affinity capability with the supported June 2026 findings and an explicit freshness boundary.
change_log.reason: The supplied review did not independently verify the broader characterization or subsequent developments.

change_log.change: Integrated prespecified definitions, conditions, thresholds, uncertainty criteria, computational costs and independent reproducibility into the proposed demonstration.
change_log.reason: These additions make the proposed capability assessable without presenting new thresholds as established standards.

change_log.reason: The final interpretation must reflect the supplied review’s actual evidentiary reach.

unresolved_issues: Field-wide progress after the June 2026 study remains unverified; the supplied freshness-search record was empty.
The supplied evidence does not determine current capability across protein–protein partners, disordered targets, membrane-associated targets or varying environmental conditions.
Binding-versus-nonbinding discrimination remains unevaluated for the five benchmarked pipelines in the supplied study.
Performance on genuinely unfamiliar targets remains uncertain because all benchmark structures predated the AlphaFold3 training cutoff; actual training-set membership is not resolved here.
Numerical success thresholds, binding definitions, acceptable computational costs and required proteome coverage remain to be specified for the proposed demonstration.
Supplementary material and figure images were not inspected in the supplied review and could contain relevant details beyond its main-text account.
